lean_implies_source.reasoning: The restricted integral is E[g²1_{g>t}] for any g with law standardNormalLaw. The Lean equality uses the closed-tail mass P{g≥t}, but gaussianReal 0 1 is atomless, hence P{g≥t}=P{g>t}. After this harmless replacement, both the exact identity and bound are exactly the source display for every t≥1.

source_implies_lean.reasoning: Applying the source exercise to a variable with law gaussianReal 0 1 converts its expectation to the restricted-law integral. Atomlessness gives equality of the source strict-tail probability with standardNormalLaw.real (Ici t), yielding the target equality; the source's chained bound yields the target inequality with identical constants.

rationale: The target faithfully expresses Exercise 2.1.4 at the level of the standard-normal law. Mathlib's gaussianReal 0 1 uses mean zero and variance one, so its density normalization is exactly exp(-x²/2)/sqrt(2π). The restricted Ioi integral is the strict-tail truncated second moment, and all constants, exponents, threshold conditions, equality, and upper bound match. Although the probability term uses the closed tail Ici t while the source writes the strict tail, the nondegenerate standard normal has zero mass at every singleton, making the two probabilities identical. Thus both implication directions hold without loss or strengthening.
